What's the difference between let, const, and var in JavaScript?
ZAK AI2:34 PM
Great question! Here are the key differences:

  • var — function-scoped, hoisted, can be redeclared
  • let — block-scoped, not hoisted, cannot be redeclared
  • const — block-scoped, not hoisted, cannot be reassigned

Best practice: Use const by default, let when reassignment is needed.

Message with Code Block

AI message containing a formatted code block.

ZAK AI2:35 PM
Here's a React useEffect example:
useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();

  async function fetchData() {
    const res = await fetch(url, {
      signal: controller.signal
    });
    const data = await res.json();
    setData(data);
  }

  fetchData();
  return () => controller.abort();
}, [url]);
The cleanup function aborts the fetch on unmount.

JavaScript

Copy message content to clipboard.

HTML
document.querySelectorAll('.zak-copy-msg').forEach(btn => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', function() {
        const bubble = this.closest('.zak-ai-cmsg-body').querySelector('.zak-ai-cmsg-bubble');
        if (bubble) {
            navigator.clipboard.writeText(bubble.textContent.trim());
            this.innerHTML = 'âœ“ Copied';
            setTimeout(() => {
                this.innerHTML = '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">...</svg> Copy';
            }, 2000);
        }
    });
});
